placements.why: The content is about knowledge management as an organizational practice — specifically the directed excision of knowledge from the record. No existing strata category covers knowledge governance; the listed examples (Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates/Calibration) do not include it. This content calls for a new organizational category to hold knowledge-governance narratives.
placements.title: Knowledge as a governed organizational asset
placements.theme: The organization treats its knowledge record as something it actively governs — including the authority to excise knowledge entirely.

placements.title: From Record to Erasure
placements.theme: The organization directs the complete removal of knowledge from its record and retroactively denies the excised activity ever occurred.
placements.why: All three segments express a unified posture of knowledge excision: two directives command removal of all knowledge about the Kestrelwood spectrograph and its calibration, and the assertive retroactively denies the observatory ever performed the calibration. No existing narrative leaf holds this theme. The grain test admits it — this names a subject (how the organization handles knowledge it determines should no longer exist) that future envelopes could keep feeding, not a one-time fact.
